Hi,

I'm a lecturer in Analysis at Loughborough University (PhD from Imperial). My research is in Spectral Theory and Mathematical Physics.

I learned Lean over the last few months with the aim of contributing to mathlib. I worked my way through MIL and its exercises as well as the Real Analysis game (which nicely overlapped with the Analysis module I am teaching).

I am still trying to get an overview of what already exists in Analysis/Spectral Theory and trying to find small parts where I could contribute. Any pointers would of course be much appreciated.

Lukas
@Laura Monk has a background in spectral theory

Hi and welcome! My background is in differential geometry, so I'm happy to answer questions about all things manifolds and mathlib. I'm not an expert on spectral geometry, though - so will let Laura speak.

Hi Lukas, it is nice to see that more people with an analysis background are getting interested in Lean.
I will try to mention a few things that we have and what we are lacking: on the having side is some spectral theory of compact operators: docs#ContinuousLinearMap.orthogonalComplement_iSup_eigenspaces_eq_bot, the Rayleigh quotient: docs#ContinuousLinearMap.rayleighQuotient, the resolvent for bounded operators is docs#resolvent, some unbounded operator theory, e.g., the adjoint is docs#LinearPMap.adjoint, the resolvent for unbounded operators will be added in the next couple of days (maybe even today).
There is some work in progress by @Yoh Tanimoto and @Oliver Butterley on the spectral theorem for bounded operators. I don't know about the progress there and how well it integrates into the unbounded operator theory.
For applications, we have the Hs,p(Rn)H^{s,p}(\mathbb{R}^n)Hs,p(Rn) Sobolev spaces, docs#BesselPotentialSpace, there is a project by Michael, Floris, and Filippo on Wk,p(Ω)W^{k,p}(\Omega)Wk,p(Ω).
I have some code on Hs(Ω)H^{s}(\Omega)Hs(Ω) for Ω\OmegaΩ open and the Laplacian on Rn\mathbb{R}^nRn as an unbounded self-adjoint operator at https://github.com/mcdoll/DirichletProblem/blob/master/DirichletProblem/Sobolev/SpectralTheoryLaplacian.lean (using the standard criterion for self-adjointness)
I think there is also a bit on graph Laplacians, but I am not familiar with that bit of mathlib (or the mathematics).

So what is missing and what would be good projects? I would like to see more on unbounded operator side, perturbation theory results, projection valued measures (might be in Yoh and Oliver's project already), the spectrum, etc. For concrete applications, I would assume that the spectral theory (in the strict sense) is not the limiting factor currently.

Hi Moritz, thank you, this is very helpful. I will have a look at docs#LinearPMap.adjoint and your code on the Dirichlet Laplacian.

The unbounded operator topic aligns very well with my own research. I'd be quite interested in contributing towards establishing the Friedrichs extension. I can see that Lax--Milgram is already there, though as far as I can tell over R\mathbb{R}R only.
The Friedrichs extension would be a great project, I would assume everything you need for it is there

hello, sorry that I've been slow with the spectral theorem. we are following Rudin's "Real and complex analyis" for complex/vector measures and "Functional analysis" for the spectral theorem.

we have a project here https://github.com/oliver-butterley/SpectralThm but the pieces are scattered, I did some stuff related with vector measures directly to mathlib, while I wrote the definition of projection-valued measure (resolution of identity) in the project but I still need to define the L^\infty space associated with it (Rudin FA section 12.20), and actually it seemed to me it's best to make some modification to it...

Just currently I'm teaching a lot, but I hope to have more time for Lean from the middle of October. I would be happy to receive comments, especially if you are familiar with Rudin's books.

Hi Yoh, thank you for the overview. I really like Rudin's Functional Analysis book. It's my standard reference and I have used it for teaching. I will have a look and let you know if I have any comments.
